entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Paterius was a sixth–seventh-century bishop of Brescia and a scholarly compiler best known for assembling excerpts from the works of Pope Gregory the Great. Having served in Gregory’s administrative circle in Rome before his episcopate, he produced florilegia that organised Gregorian teachings for pastoral and studious use—an early example of the excerpt culture that transmitted late antique papal theology into Lombard Italy and beyond.

In an age when full manuscript copies were scarce, Paterius’s compilations helped stabilise Gregory’s authority as a doctor of the Latin church. His career links Roman papal bureaucracy to northern Italian episcopal chairs during the Lombard period, showing how Gregorian thought travelled through trusted clerks turned bishops. Though not a major original theologian, he is significant as a vector of textual transmission in early medieval Italy.
